elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted 7(d) says only "Contractor shall indemnify Company"; there is no "defend" (or hold harmless) obligation and no reference to Company's affiliates anywhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 7(d) runs in favour of "Company" only; affiliates are not named as indemnified parties.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "any third-party claim that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — Works are the contract's deliverables construct (cf. 5(c) "the Works provided hereunder").

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 7(d) is confined to IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no breach-of-law trigger was added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised access/disclosure of Company data limb appears in 7(d) or elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 7(d) contains no allocation of defence control (consistent with there being no defence obligation at all).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation in the inserted text.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the Agreement contains no Company indemnity of Contractor (Section 7 holds only liability caps and an attorneys'-fees waiver), so there is no broader Customer indemnity to narrow.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New 7(d): "Contractor shall indemnify Company against any third-party claim that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "except to the extent the claim arises from Company's modification of the Services or Works".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "from combination of the Services or Works with items not supplied by Contractor".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall procure for Company the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing" — expressed as a mandatory obligation.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is commercially available, Contractor shall refund the fees paid for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding Paragraph 7(a), Contractor's aggregate liability under this Paragraph 7(d) shall not exceed three times (3x) the annual fees paid to Contractor under this Agreement."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: every one of the seven fallback elements is present in operative language in new Section 7(d), including all three customary exclusions, the mandatory procure/modify/replace ladder, the refund backstop, and an express 3x annual-fees super-cap.

Preferred level is not reached: no duty to defend, no affiliates as indemnified parties, no breach-of-law / data-breach / gross-negligence-or-wilful-misconduct limbs, and no notice, defence-control or cooperation procedure. The Customer-indemnity element is met only vacuously because the Agreement imposes no indemnity on Company.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion after the existing 7(c), deletes nothing, and adds no survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate outside the fallback checklist. The narrow "Notwithstanding Paragraph 7(a)" carve-out is necessary rather than surplus, because without it the 7(a) fees-paid cap would swallow the required 3x super-cap; it is targeted at the specific cap rather than a broad override.

Intent is preserved: the 7(a) and 7(b) allocations, the Paragraph 9 carve-out and the 7(c) attorneys'-fees waiver survive without contradiction; the Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty is complementary, and the terms used (Services, Works, Company, Contractor) are already defined in the Agreement, leaving no dangling reference.

Drafting nit for the drafter, not a fallback failure: because 7(d) says "indemnify" only and omits defence costs/attorneys' fees, the retained 7(c) waiver could be argued to limit recovery of Company's own fees in a covered third-party suit; if a preferred-level push is available, add "defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates ... including reasonable attorneys' fees" plus notice/control/cooperation.
